summary: Buchanan County tower at 2,250 ft: a 110-foot Aermotor built in the early 1930s on the Coal Heritage Trail; standing, run by a named individual, on the Register since 2017.

events.note: Register gives only 'early 1930s'; 1930 stands in for that period, not a confirmed year

evidence.supports: 110-foot Aermotor tower built in the early 1930s
evidence.quote: This 110' Aermotor tower was built in the early 1930s.

evidence.supports: sits atop the Coal Heritage Trail; sister tower Bearwallow
evidence.quote: Like its sister tower, Bearwallow Tower, High Knob Leemaster sits atop the Coal Heritage Trail in southwestern Virginia.

evidence.supports: administrator is a named individual, not an agency
Leemaster is an unincorporated community in Buchanan County
evidence.quote: Leemaster is an unincorporated community in Buchanan County, Virginia , United States.

evidence.supports: post office at Leemaster ran 1905 to 1972
evidence.quote: A post office was established at Leemaster in 1905, and remained in operation until it was discontinued in 1972.

evidence.supports: other High Knob towers in Rockingham County
other High Knob tower in Wise County

corrections.proposed: remove from agency; record the administrator as a named individual, not an agency
corrections.why: The Register's 'Administered by' field names a person, not an agency

notes_for_editor: Thin record. Build date is 'early 1930s' only; no staffing, fire or access information in any source. The Register names a named individual as administrator (the same name appears as administrator on the Bearwallow record), so the story refers to an individual without naming them. The Forest Lookouts page for this tower was not in the cache. Not to be confused with the High Knob towers in Rockingham and Wise counties, which are separate records.
